title: How do you implement blue-green deployments in an API Gateway (weighted routing)?
shortTitle: How to implement blue-green deployments in an API Gateway
keyPoints: Blue-green runs two complete production environments side by side: blue (current) and green (new).
The gateway uses weighted routing to shift traffic gradually from blue to green.
Rollback is instant: shift the weight back to blue, which never stopped running.
Both environments must share compatible data during the overlap (expand-and-contract migrations).
Blue-green differs from canary (small user slice for observation) and rolling update (gradual in-place replacement).
Weight changes should run through an audited, automated pipeline for safety.
The release is a traffic decision, not a deployment, which is why cutover and rollback are so fast.

s1_definition.oneliner: Blue-green runs old and new side by side and uses gateway weighted routing to shift traffic gradually from blue to green, with instant rollback by shifting the weights back.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Blue-green deployment** – runs two complete production environments simultaneously, blue (current) and green (new), and switches traffic between them.
- **Weighted routing** – the gateway sends a configurable percentage of traffic to each environment (e.g., 90% blue, 10% green).
- **Instant rollback** – shift weight back to blue, which never stopped running; no rebuild or redeploy needed.
- **Data compatibility** – during overlap, both versions must read and write compatible data (expand-and-contract migrations).
- **Release as traffic decision** – because both environments are already deployed, the release is just a route change, not a deployment.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine National Bank of India opens a brand-new banking hall (green) right next to the existing one (blue), both fully staffed. The manager at the entrance directs customers. At first everyone goes to the trusted blue hall. Then a few customers are quietly sent to green. If green works, more go there, until everyone is in green and blue is closed. If anything goes wrong in green, the manager instantly waves all customers back to blue.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Blue-Green Deployment via Gateway
  ──────────────────────────────────
  Incoming Traffic
       │
       ▼
  ┌──────────────────┐
  │   API Gateway     │
  │  Weight Routing   │
  └──┬────────────┬──┘
     │            │
     │ 90%        │ 10%
     ▼            ▼
  ┌────────┐  ┌────────┐
  │ Blue   │  │ Green  │
  │ (v1.0) │  │ (v2.0) │
  └────┬───┘  └───┬────┘
       │          │
       └────┬─────┘
            ▼
     Shared Database
     (compatible schema)

  Rollout: 100/0 → 90/10 → 50/50 → 0/100
  Rollback: any step → 100/0 (instant)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A blue-green deployment runs two complete production environments at the same time and releases by switching traffic from one to the other. At the gateway, this is implemented with weighted routing: two routes for the same path, each with a configurable weight, and the gateway picks a backend in proportion to those weights. Because both environments are already deployed and healthy, the release is just a traffic decision, which is what makes both the cutover and the rollback extremely fast.

At National Bank of India, Pankaj released a new account service with zero downtime. He started at 100% blue, shifted to 90/10 with automated metric checks, then 50/50, and finally 100% green. When a canary slice showed elevated latency on a previous release, the pipeline automatically shifted back to 100% blue in seconds. Blue never stopped running, so the rollback was a single weight change with no rebuild or outage.

The nuances are data compatibility and pipeline safety. During the overlap, both versions must read and write compatible data, which requires expand-and-contract migrations. Weight changes must run through an audited, automated pipeline so an accidental shift of payment traffic to a broken version is prevented and always instantly reversible.

Remember one sentence: blue-green uses gateway weighted routing to shift traffic gradually from old to new, with instant rollback by shifting the weights back, because both environments are always running.
